name: In-situ Medusa-GCMS measurement of atmospheric halocarbons, PFCs, SF6 and NMHCs with dual adsorbent traps cooled to -165 C by a Cryotiger
plain_name: Monitor ozone-depleting and greenhouse gases at a remote air station
description: Two-litre whole-air samples are preconcentrated on adsorbent micro-traps cooled to -165 C by a closed-cycle Cryotiger cooler, selectively flushed at -70/-125 C to remove CO2, Xe and bulk air, desorbed at +100 C and transferred to a GC-MS, giving 12 air measurements per day of PFCs, SF6, HFCs, HCFCs, CFCs and halons at AGAGE stations.
keywords: Monitor ozone-depleting and greenhouse gases at a remote air station

sources.citation: Medusa-GCMS - Atmospheric Chemistry Research Group instruments, University of Bristol

requirements.rationale: Adsorbent traps must reach -165 C (108.15 K) to retain the most volatile species.
Each cycle runs the trap between -165 C trapping and +100 C desorption.
Preconcentrated analytes are separated and detected by the coupled GC-MS.
